resources.title: Comparing celebrations
paragraphs_in_document_order: Thursday 3 December 2026 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A

Teach one forty-minute comparison lesson to three or four pupils. Use two fictional, unnamed community examples. Pupils find one similarity and one difference, using evidence from both cards. The comparison is about what people do and share; it does not rank beliefs, groups or ways of taking part.

Outcome verbatim: Compare how different communities celebrate. Source: BUILD Weekly - Autumn!B54/C54, originally Autumn 2 Week 2. The owner moves this outcome to taught Week 5, Thursday 3 December 2026, P3. C57 remembrance moved to Week 2; C55 stayed in Week 3. Keep source row and taught order distinct.

Theme: Identity & Belonging. Unit: Festivals & beliefs, light around the world. Term assessment: F: participation and recognition.  S: festival comparison task (Dec). This lesson provides formative comparison evidence for the wider sequence; it is not labelled as the final assessing lesson.

Put Support Cards page 1, source cards A and B, the word mat and visible model at each seat. Supply books and usual aids. The starter compares simple printed marks before moving to the celebration examples. No group question is needed. Use anonymous codes learner–learner only.

One similarity and one difference that compare the same feature across both examples. All routes retain a word bank, sentence starters and visible model at each task. Level 2 is the requested scaffold provision, not a qualification level. Pupils can point, draw, match, write or direct an exact scribe.

A and B are fictional labels, not real names. Communities are described by their shared activity: meeting to mark a special day. These short examples do not represent every person or celebration. Some people join; others watch or choose another way. No pupil must reveal a belief, describe home traditions or speak for a group.
Thursday 3 December 2026 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A
2 minutes private settle; 8 minutes simple same/different starter and quiet check-ins.
5 minutes source teaching with brief reset; 5 minutes model and private hinge; 5 minutes guided comparison.
10 minutes individual book comparison with a reset; 3 minutes private feedback; 2 minutes exit.

“These are two made-up examples. Each group marks a special day. We can look at what people do and share. We can find something the same and something different. Different does not mean better or worse. Use both cards. You can point or ask me to write.”

Same: “Both groups share stories.” Difference in the featured activity: “In A, some sing. In B, some draw.” Point to the matching evidence in A and B. A useful alternative difference is paper lanterns and cloth flags, both in the decoration category.

Ask privately “Show evidence from A and B.” If a response mentions only one card, re-read one matched line from each and offer two choices. Then use the parallel check “Do these compare the same feature?” Re-model if a pupil compares a decoration with a story. Do not ask for a show of hands or a public answer.

Accept HELP/PASS, a quiet request or the usual aid. Offer supported reading, pointing to a source, adult scribing or an agreed supervised pause. Do not require a reason in front of others. Record evidence gaps honestly; willingness to talk publicly is not a learning criterion.
Thursday 3 December 2026 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A

Supported: match the story lines, then select a paired difference and direct a scribe. Independent: record one similarity and one matched-feature difference in a book. Aspire: add another comparison or a question the cards cannot answer. All routes use the same source cards, word banks, stems and visible models. A question is not an invented answer.

Pupil selects the source words or says their response. Adult records exact words or labels and reads them back quietly for keep/change. Record adult-supplied ideas and prompts. Do not infer independent reading, writing or comparison from copying the model.

Cognition: one short step and paired source lines. Communication: quiet wait time, exact scribe, usual aid, plan in any language. SEMH: predictable routine and private pass. Sensory/physical: large print, stable desk layout and usual equipment. Words, marks and position carry meaning without colour.

Use HUM-BUILD-A2-W05-E1. Check one similarity, one difference with A and B, source evidence and actual help. Record part shown or not yet shown where appropriate. Actual audience reply, one NS and own-colour or usual supported response precede R. Actual banking precedes E. Leave actual attendance, delivery and outcomes blank until they occur.

An event helper listens to different choices and finds shared needs without assuming everyone wants the same thing. Offer authentic pupil words or choices to the Communication portfolio. [AWARD] / [QUAL] checks remain separate.

resources.title: Staff guidance and checks
paragraphs_in_document_order: Thursday 3 December 2026 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A

Compare how different communities celebrate. From BUILD Weekly - Autumn!B54/C54, originally Week 2, moved to taught Week 5 by the owner. Thursday 3 December 2026, P3. Theme: Identity & Belonging. The separate remembrance move is C57 to W2; C55 remains W3. This is formative evidence, not a qualification decision.

Both examples meet to mark a special day, share stories and allow joining or watching. Any one accurate shared feature is valid. The model is “Both groups share stories.” Pupils must refer to evidence from both A and B.

Compare like with like. Featured activity: in A some sing; in B some draw pictures. Decoration: A uses paper lanterns; B uses cloth flags. Either paired difference is valid. Accept selected labels, exact scribing or a clear drawn/pointed comparison. A feature from one card alone is not yet a comparison.

These are fictional examples, not claims about named communities. Do not infer that everyone takes part in the same way, or that A never draws or B never sings. The cards highlight activities; missing information is not evidence of never. No ranking of groups or request for personal belief is needed.

A second comparison can use the decoration pair. An unanswered question can be “What story do they share?” No answer is supplied, so do not invent one. If a pupil compares lanterns with stories, return to one shared category. If they say “Different means worse,” explain that different ways can be treated with equal respect.
Thursday 3 December 2026 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A
Use learner only if a fourth pupil attends. Leave absent pupils blank. Keep each response individual, even after shared matching.

Look for one accurate similarity, one difference about a matched feature, and evidence from A and B. Pointing is valid when the pupil selects both relevant lines. If an adult supplies the comparison, record that support rather than implying an independent outcome.

Word bank, sentence starters and visible model stay on every task. Scribe exact words or labels, read back privately for keep/change and record help. No public questioning or required reading aloud. Offer usual aids, supported observation or an agreed supervised pause.

Use HUM-BUILD-A2-W05-E1. Offer authentic words or choices to the Communication portfolio. R follows actual audience reply, one NS and the pupil’s own response; E follows actual banking.
